summary: Barry Kerzin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley, USC, and Keck School of Medicine, and under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. His posts include Assistant Professor of Medicine at the University of Washington and adjunct professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Barry Sautman specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. He earned degrees at UCLA, NYU, and Columbia University. He served as an adjunct assistant professor at California State University, Northridge, a visiting assistant professor at the Hopkins-Nanjing Center, and an assistant professor at HKUST.
Bart Dessein works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied under Charles Willemen and serves as an Associate Professor at Ghent University (attested 2014–2026).
Bart Gruzalski specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Maryland, College Park, and served as a professor of philosophy at Northeastern University.

Barthold Georg Niebuhr was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Kiel University. He held chairs (Lehrstuhl) at the Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1810 to 1813 and the University of Bonn from circa 1823 to 1831.

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He served as Professor of Greek at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Professor at Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

Bazar Baradiyn was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at Saint Petersburg State University. He taught at Saint Petersburg State University and headed both the Mongolian Academy of Sciences and the Buryat Scientific Center.

Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. at Stanford University. She was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley and served as Associate Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Washington University in St. Louis.

Beatrice Lane Suzuki worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe College and Columbia University under William James, Josiah Royce, George Santayana, and George Herbert Palmer, and was appointed professor at Otani University in 1921.

Beatrix Pfleiderer worked in Indology and medical anthropology, studying at the University of Maryland and Heidelberg University. She held positions at the University of Maryland, Heidelberg University, the University of Hamburg, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the European University Viadrina.

Bedřich Hrozný was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding posts at the University of Vienna (1905–1919) and Charles University (circa 1919–1952).
Beihō Takashima was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University from circa 1896 to 1901 and later held a post there.

Bela Bhattacharya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She has held posts as Professor in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and as Professor at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Ben Jiao specializes in Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein and served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2008).
Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan (attested 2019).

Benedetta Lomi specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London and held teaching positions at the University of Virginia (circa 2014–2017) and the University of Bristol (circa 2018).

Benimadhab Barua worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at institutions including Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of London. He served as Lecturer in Pali (1913–1914) and Professor (1918–1948) at the University of Calcutta.

Benjamin A. Elman is a historian and sinologist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He held faculty posts at Colby College, UCLA, and Princeton University, where he directed the East Asian Studies Program.

Benjamin Bogin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr., and also studied under Janet Gyatso, Gareth Sparham, and Lopon Ugyen Rinpoche.

Benjamin Brose specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his Ph.D. at Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and became an assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan circa 2009.
